history.dynasty: Unknown (tribal folk shrine; build date unpublished)
history.period: Worship site said to be established ~90 years ago (~1930s, per local legend)
history.summary: Hilltop temple complex on the Longtharai hill range in Dhalai district, near Ambassa; 'Longtharai' is the Kokborok name of Lord Shiva, and the temple is described as the most revered religious site in Dhalai district, drawing both tribal and non-tribal devotees. Per local legend the worship site was established about 90 years ago when a man was beckoned to build a temple at the hilltop; devotees, including many students, trek up in February for the annual puja. IDENTITY CAVEAT: multiple shrines named Longtharai/Longtrai exist in Tripura — the hilltop cluster described here, a 'Baba Longtarai Mandir (Hapong Raja)' listing in Manu Block (~9 km from Ambassa), and a 'Longtarai Temple' listing at Chailengta on NH-108. Coordinates come from map.geocode's top match (Chailengta listing) and are approximate — verify on the ground which shrine the CSV intends.

name: Longtharai Mandir
town_description: Ambassa is the district headquarters of Dhalai district in central Tripura, a municipal town on the National Highway between Agartala and the northern districts; it is the gateway to the Longtharai hill range, the Dumboor lake region and the tribal heartland of the state.
tradition: Shaivism with Tripuri tribal folk worship

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~102 km per travel vlogs)
travel.road: The temple is reached by road from Ambassa; the hilltop shrine involves a climb of steps from the base of the Longtharai hills

visitor_information.best_time: February, when the annual Longtharai Puja draws large crowds; otherwise the cooler dry months (October–March)
visitor_information.opening_hours: No published timings — daylight visits typical for the hilltop shrine (verify locally)
